name: Operating a high-operating-temperature (HOT) T2SL MWIR focal-plane array at about 120 K in a vacuum dewar cooled by a linear Stirling cryocooler (integrated dewar cooler assembly)
plain_name: Keep a thermal-sight camera's infrared chip near 120 K inside a sealed vacuum package with a long-life cooler
description: Cooled MWIR camera modules (Teledyne FLIR Neutrino) put the focal-plane array, cold shield and cold filter in a vacuum dewar with hermetically sealed electrical feedthroughs, cooled by a mechanical linear cryocooler (FL-100) in an Integrated Dewar Cooler Assembly. HOT barrier (T2SL) detectors operate at approximately 120 K, versus about 77 K for InSb and most HgCdTe; the FL-100 MTTF is about 27,000 h from lifetime tests and Weibull analysis.
keywords: Keep a thermal-sight camera's infrared chip near 120 K inside a sealed vacuum package with a long-life cooler

sources.citation: Teledyne FLIR, Understanding Cryocooled Infrared System Reliability (white paper, Rev. 100, 2021)

requirements.rationale: The HOT barrier FPA operates at approximately 120 K.
The FPA is housed in a vacuum dewar.
Infrared photons must reach the FPA through the cold shield and cold filter.
ROIC signals leave the dewar through hermetic electrical feedthroughs.
Cooling is by a mechanical cryocooler integrated with the dewar; no liquid cryogen in the field.
